_comment: STING panel schedule template selection rules. Board -> template: first by what the board IS (ElectricalEquipment.IsSwitchboard, supply phases; data panels by name) via PanelBoardProfile, then by these name rules, matched against both the Panel Name and the family type name. The STING standard templates these rules name are BUILT by 'Panel templates -> Create / update' from STING_PANEL_SCHEDULE_SPECS.json.
_apiNotes: PanelScheduleTemplate.Create(doc, PanelScheduleType, PanelConfiguration, name) creates templates, and GetTableData/SetTableData + TableSectionData edit them (insert/remove rows and columns, bind cells to parameters, text, widths) - verified against the Revit 2025 API reference on 2026-09-24. The earlier note that the API cannot edit template structure was wrong.
PanelScheduleSheetInstance.Create is reported broken in Revit 2024/2025/2026 (not re-verified) - STING does not place panel schedules on sheets; drag the views on manually.
PanelConfiguration values: OneColumn, TwoColumnsCircuitsAcross, TwoColumnsCircuitsDown. PanelScheduleType values: Branch, Switchboard, Data.

rules._comment: Switchboard / main distribution — wide template with utility, summary rows, multi-section support
Sub-main / distribution boards — three-phase branch with summary + load classification
Single-phase consumer units / final circuit boards
Data / comms cabinets — communications panel layout (no breaker columns)
Catch-all branch panel rule — applies when no name pattern matches

globalFallback._comment: If no rule matches AND none of the templates in matched rules exist, use the first PanelScheduleTemplate in the project as last-resort.

skipPatterns._comment: Panel name patterns to skip entirely (e.g., spare panels, placeholders, future loads).
